Description: UDP port players join on

Language of these settings in AMP and of the texts the server itself produces. Players see the mod in their own game language. After a change run install-into-amp.sh again (or reload the instance) so AMP shows the fields in the new language.

The world the server runs: the worlds on this server, or "(world played last)". The server fills the list itself; AMP shows new worlds after the next restart of the instance. A new world comes from "New world: name" (tab New world); on a server without any world, "New world: difficulty" creates one called "Server".

Load this save at the next start instead of the newest, once - later restarts load the newest again. The list shows the saves on this server, newest first, with game day and time; the server fills it itself, AMP shows new saves after the next restart of the instance. "(newest save)" = always the newest.

Create a new world with this name: at the next start the server creates it with the difficulty below, confirms character creation with 'Server character name' and plays it. Afterwards it is a world like any other - keep 'World' on '(world played last)' to stay in it. Empty = no new world; a name that exists already just keeps that world, so use a new name for each new world.

Difficulty of a new world: the one named in 'New world: name', or the world set above while it does not exist yet. Easy, Normal and Hard are the game's own presets; Custom uses the values on the 'Custom' tab, like the game's 'Custom Game' screen. Off = no new world.
How many days a game year has: 30-365. Only for 'Custom'. Normal: 60.
Money every new character starts with. Only for 'Custom'. Easy 15000, Normal 10000, Hard 4200.

18-65. Only for 'Custom'. Normal: 18.

Vehicles use no fuel. Only for 'Custom'.

Name of the host character that keeps the world running
How many players may be on the server at once (the server's own character does not count). AMP shows it as the user limit on the status page.
Seconds after the last player left before the world pauses (0 = at once).

DisplayName: Pause when every player is idle for (minutes)
Description: The world pauses while no connected player has used keyboard or mouse for this many minutes, and resumes on the next input. 0 = off. A running time skip is never paused.

DisplayName: Pause while every player is in the pause menu
Description: The world pauses while every connected player has the game's pause menu (Esc) open - with one player like in single player.

DisplayName: Join only with the server key
Description: Players who do not enter the server key are refused. Off = anyone who can reach the server can join.

DisplayName: Warning before AMP stops the server
Description: When AMP stops, restarts or updates the server (its buttons and the schedule) while players are on, they are warned first - at 60, 30 and 10 seconds - and the world is saved after. 0 = at once. At most 90 (AMP waits 150 seconds for the server). For a longer warning, send "restart <minutes>" in the console or from the schedule.

DisplayName: Steam: only players who own the game
Description: Lets in only players whose Steam account owns Big Ambitions: the server asks Steam about a ticket each player's game sends when joining - a Steam emulator cannot make one; Family Sharing counts. Needs the Steam Web API key below. If Steam does not answer, the player is let in and the log says so.

For the ownership check: a key from steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey (any Steam account that has bought something on Steam can create one; any domain name will do). It stays on this server and never goes to the players.

Players on this server tell Steam where they play: their Steam friends see Join Game and Invite to Game and get onto this server with one click - the address and the server key go to them over Steam. Not for players connected by a local (LAN) address. Off = no Join Game for this server.
Players who join a running world are let in without approval
How often the server saves the world automatically. Players see "Saving the game on the server..." and then whether it worked.
How many automatic saves the server keeps per world; the oldest is overwritten. Manual and disconnect saves are extra.
Frames per second of the server while players are on it: 60, 120 or 200. More frames make the world react faster (more CPU); the network sends on its own clock either way.
Frame cap while the world waits (paused, no players): low saves CPU, joins still respond.

How often positions, cars and traffic go over the network: Normal (positions 10 Hz, traffic 5 Hz, as before 1.0.14), High (20 / 10 Hz), Very high (30 / 15 Hz) or Maximum (60 / 30 Hz). Higher is smoother while driving; every player's stream goes to every other player, so the traffic grows quickly with more players. The players get the server's level when they join.

What the world does when a player loses the connection (a timeout, not leaving): Off - the others play on, his cars stay; Up to 60 seconds - it waits a minute for a quick reconnect; Until the player returns - as before 1.0.16.
Players whose Going Public Server version differs from the server's are refused with a message naming both versions. Off: they can join and get a note in the chat to update.
Normal: the console shows what matters (joins, saves, warnings, errors) - the frequent status lines of the systems are left out. Detailed: everything, for finding a fault.

The players' games send this server their errors, warnings and the mod's check lines while they play - only after each player agreed once (asked when joining, changeable under Options, tab Mods), without Windows user names, IP addresses, Steam IDs and keys. After a crash, or asked with the console command playerlog <player>, the whole Player.log too. Files in bigambitions/player-reports (summary.json, one file per player and day, logs/), kept 14 days; every 10 minutes one line in the console, the console command reports lists the most frequent errors. Off = nothing is sent.

Translates the players' chat between German and English, on this server itself: no account, no service on the internet - the chat never leaves the server. Each player reads foreign-language lines in the language of their game, with the original small below; each player can switch it off under Options, tab Mods. The first start sets the translator up once in bigambitions/bamp-translate (about 550 MB download, outside the game folder, so not in the backups) - the game starts at once, the translation follows within minutes. About 400 MB of memory while the server runs. Console command translate <text> for a test. Off = chat as written, nothing is set up or started.

Players need this key to join (Join a Game > Server key) and to open the ranking page. Empty = one is created on first start, shown on the status page and kept in telemetry-data/key.txt.
Where players reach this AMP panel, e.g. https://amp.example.org or http://203.0.113.5:8080 - used for the server's mod list. Empty = https://<the address players join>.
Module 1: players can call the Internal Revenue Service in the phone's contacts and pay their taxes there.
Module 2: players put their own pictures on their shop signs and billboards; the other players see them.
Module 3: a third-person camera on foot and in the car. On this server every player gets the settings in 'RPG camera'; the camera's own settings window only shows them.
Module 4: schedule checks, the game's own auto-fill and opening hours by customer demand for the players' own businesses.
Module 5: the books of the players' businesses and buildings - profit, history, staff, sales and real estate.
Module 6: a destination from the search, your places, bookmarks or a click on the city map, with the route line on foot and in the car. Only each player's own view.

Module 7: the BizPhone's apps in pages of eight with arrows and dots - the game's on the first page, the mod's on the next (Chat, Business, Radio, Navigation, Planner, Insights, camera, shop signs). Modelled on Aluna's Phone Pages. Off = the phone as before: the game's apps, Chat and Business.

Module 8: every player can found a cable network operator - a business of the game ("Cable provider" in a warehouse, "Cable customer center" in an office, founded in BizMan), against the competitor Skyline Cable: buy bandwidth, connect buildings, sell internet, TV (cable and IPTV) and phone lines with tariffs, rented or bought devices and number porting. The equipment (CMTS, OLT, satellite head-end ...) is furniture from the furniture store, the devices are goods at wholesalers and importers, the staff in six roles come from the recruitment agencies; permission contracts with the owners, faults and customer satisfaction; DOCSIS 3.0, later 3.1 and fiber with XGS-PON. The app is in the phone and in the full menu (Shift+F12), help under F1; the ranking page lists the players' providers. Each player's provider is kept in that player's save. Off = the app is gone; a provider founded before stays in the saves.

Module 9: three office businesses of the game - IT Support, Software Development, Cloud Services. The staff (IT support, software developers, cloud engineers from City Workforce Inc.) bill hours at IT workplaces; servers (blade, rack, mainframe) from the furniture store must stand in the office and cost power every day. Prices and shifts in BizMan, help under F1. Modelled on IT Business Expansion by Cow a Bunga (our own code). Off = these businesses earn nothing.

Module 10: a cleaning company (office) of the game. Its cleaners and crew leads clean the player's own other businesses first, then clients of the city pay by the hour; floor scrubbers, carpet extractors and window kits make the crews faster. Prices and shifts in BizMan, help under F1. Modelled on Spotless by We1tall (our own code). Off = the crews do nothing.

Module 11: a laundromat (shop) of the game: washers (8, 12 and 27 kg) and dryers (15 and 30 kg) from the appliance store, people of the neighbourhood wash and dry, with an attendant they leave their laundry for wash and fold. Water, power and detergent cost a little per load. Prices and shifts in BizMan, help under F1. Modelled on Spotless by We1tall (our own code). Off = nobody washes.
Shows the route line for every player on this server. Off = only the pin with the distance and the destination at the top.

While a destination is set, the sat-nav fills the BizPhone's screen below the music player - with the mouse over it the phone's apps show through and can be clicked; a collapsed phone shows no sat-nav. Off = it stands on top of the phone.

Internet radio for every player on this server: the station list in this language comes from GitHub (radio/<language>.txt at github.com/amaus1209/BigAmbitionsGoingPublicServer) and shows in the phone's Radio app and on the car radio - MP3 streams, http and https. The players' own streams.txt comes first. Off = only their own.

A member of a merged company who has not been on the server for this many days (counted only while the server runs, from this update on) leaves the company by themselves - without the vote and the sale: everybody keeps their own property, the company's money is split equally, and a merger of two ends. Only while another member was there in that time. 0 = never.
